title: Grade 8 Composite Area and Volume: Shapes with Semicircles, Prisms and Cylinders
seo_title: Grade 8 Composite Area and Volume Worksheets: Perimeter, Area, Volume and Surface Area, Free Math with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Solve problems involving the perimeter, circumference, area, volume, and surface area of composite two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects, using appropriate formulas
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on composite shapes and solids for the Ontario curriculum: perimeter with semicircles, area of L-shapes and house shapes, volume of composite prisms and cylinders, and surface area of joined solids, with running track, pool and house problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Split a composite shape or solid into simple parts, find each part, then add (or subtract a part that is cut out).
key_sub: Perimeter counts only the outside edge, not the line where two parts meet. A semicircle is half a circle: curve π × d ÷ 2, area π × r × r ÷ 2 (π ≈ 3.14). Faces that touch are not part of the surface area.
body_html:
What a composite shape is

A composite shape is made of simple shapes: rectangles, triangles and semicircles. A composite solid is made of prisms and cylinders. To measure one, split it into parts you know, measure each part, then put the answers together.

PartPerimeter pieceArea
Rectanglethe outside sides onlyl × w
Trianglethe outside sides only½ × b × h
Semicirclecurve = π × d ÷ 2π × r × r ÷ 2

Perimeter: only the outside edge

Walk around the outside of the shape and add every length. A line where two parts meet is inside the shape, so it is not part of the perimeter. A semicircle adds only half a circle: π × d ÷ 2.

Example 1

Find the perimeter of the shape above. Use π ≈ 3.14.

Curve: 3.14 × 10 ÷ 2 = 15.7 cm. Straight sides: 10 + 12 + 12 = 34 cm. 34 + 15.7 = 49.7 cm.

Answer: 49.7 cm

Area: add or subtract the parts

Split the shape into rectangles, triangles and semicircles. Add their areas. If a part is cut out, subtract it. Often the fastest way is “big rectangle minus the missing corner.”

Example 2

Find the area of the shape in Example 1.

Rectangle: 10 × 12 = 120 cm². Semicircle: r = 5, so 3.14 × 5 × 5 ÷ 2 = 39.25 cm². 120 + 39.25.

Answer: 159.25 cm²

Volume of composite solids

Add the volumes of the parts, or subtract a part that is removed. For any prism, V = area of the front (base) × length, even when the front is a composite shape.

Example 3

A cylinder (r = 3 cm, h = 5 cm) sits on a 10 cm × 10 cm × 4 cm box. Find the total volume.

Box: 10 × 10 × 4 = 400 cm³. Cylinder: 3.14 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 141.3 cm³. 400 + 141.3.

Answer: 541.3 cm³

Surface area of composite solids

Surface area is the total area of all the outside faces. When two solids are joined, the faces that touch are hidden. Take the touching area away from both solids.

For a cylinder, the curved side unrolls into a rectangle: 2πr × h. Add the two circles: SA = 2πr² + 2πrh.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the line where two parts meet in the perimeterCount only the outside edge
Using a full circle (π × d) for a semicircleHalve it: π × d ÷ 2 and π × r × r ÷ 2
Using the diameter as rHalve the diameter first: d = 10, r = 5
Forgetting ½ for a triangleTriangle area = ½ × b × h
Using the sloped side as the height of a triangleUse the height, at a right angle to the base
Adding the surface areas of two joined solidsSubtract the touching area twice

faq.q: How do you find the perimeter of a shape with a semicircle?
faq.a: Add the straight outside sides and half of the circle’s circumference, π × d ÷ 2. Do not count the diameter where the semicircle joins the rectangle, because it is inside the shape.

faq.q: How do you find the area of a composite shape in Grade 8?
faq.a: Split the shape into rectangles, triangles and semicircles, find each area, then add them (or subtract a part that is cut out). For a semicircle use π × r × r ÷ 2 with π ≈ 3.14.

faq.q: Where is composite area and volume in the Ontario Grade 8 math curriculum?
faq.a: It is in Spatial Sense, expectation E2.3: students solve problems with the perimeter, circumference, area, volume and surface area of composite two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects.

faq.q: How do you find the surface area of two solids that are joined together?
faq.a: Add the surface areas of both solids, then subtract the area where they touch twice, once for each solid. Those faces are hidden inside the new solid.

items.q: What is the perimeter of a composite shape?
c: the distance around its outside edge
the sum of the perimeters of all its parts
the length of its longest side
items.e: Perimeter is the distance around the outside edge. Lines inside the shape, where two parts meet, are not part of it. That is why adding the perimeters of the parts gives too much.

items.q: A semicircle has a diameter d. How long is its curved edge?
items.e: A full circle has a circumference of π × d. A semicircle is half a circle, so its curved edge is π × d ÷ 2. π × r × r ÷ 2 is the area of a semicircle.

items.q: Find the length of the side marked with a red question mark.
items.e: The bottom is 13 m long and the top is only 8 m, so the missing side is 13 − 8 = 5 m.

items.q: Find the perimeter of this shape.
items.e: Find the 2 missing sides: 10 − 6 = 4 and 8 − 5 = 3. Add all 6 sides: 10 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 8 = 36 cm. Adding only the 4 labelled sides gives 29 cm.

items.q: Find the perimeter of this shape.
items.e: Find the 2 missing sides: 12 − 7 = 5 and 9 − 5 = 4. Add all 6 sides: 12 + 5 + 5 + 4 + 7 + 9 = 42 m. Adding only the 4 labelled sides gives 33 m.

items.q: Find the perimeter of this shape.
items.e: Find the 2 missing sides: 15 − 9 = 6 and 10 − 6 = 4. Add all 6 sides: 15 + 6 + 6 + 4 + 9 + 10 = 50 cm. Adding only the 4 labelled sides gives 40 cm.

items.q: Find the perimeter of this shape.
items.e: Find the 2 missing sides: 9 − 6 = 3 and 7 − 5 = 2. Add all 6 sides: 9 + 5 + 3 + 2 + 6 + 7 = 32 m. Adding only the 4 labelled sides gives 27 m.

items.q: Find the perimeter of this shape.
items.e: Find the 2 missing sides: 14 − 6 = 8 and 11 − 6 = 5. Add all 6 sides: 14 + 6 + 8 + 5 + 6 + 11 = 50 cm. Adding only the 4 labelled sides gives 37 cm.

items.q: The front of this shed is a rectangle with a triangle on top. The two sloped sides are equal. Find the perimeter.
items.e: Go around the outside: bottom 8, two walls 5 + 5, two sloped sides 5 + 5. 8 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 28 m. The dashed line is inside the shape, so do not count it.

items.q: The front of this shed is a rectangle with a triangle on top. The two sloped sides are equal. Find the perimeter.
items.e: Go around the outside: bottom 12, two walls 6 + 6, two sloped sides 10 + 10. 12 + 6 + 6 + 10 + 10 = 44 cm. The dashed line is inside the shape, so do not count it.

items.q: The front of this shed is a rectangle with a triangle on top. The two sloped sides are equal. Find the perimeter.
items.e: Go around the outside: bottom 6, two walls 4 + 4, two sloped sides 5 + 5. 6 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 5 = 24 m. The dashed line is inside the shape, so do not count it.
Curved edge: 3.14 × 10 ÷ 2 = 15.7. Add the straight side (the diameter): 15.7 + 10 = 25.7 cm.

items.q: A semicircle has a diameter of 8 m. Find its perimeter. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Curved edge: 3.14 × 8 ÷ 2 = 12.56. Add the straight side (the diameter): 12.56 + 8 = 20.56 m.
Curved edge: 3.14 × 10 ÷ 2 = 15.7. Straight sides: 10 + 12 + 12 = 34. Total: 34 + 15.7 = 49.7 cm. The top of the rectangle is inside the shape, so it is not counted.
Curved edge: 3.14 × 6 ÷ 2 = 9.42. Straight sides: 6 + 8 + 8 = 22. Total: 22 + 9.42 = 31.42 m. The top of the rectangle is inside the shape, so it is not counted.

items.q: A window is a rectangle 4 m wide and 5 m tall with a semicircle on top. Find the perimeter of the window. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Curved edge: 3.14 × 4 ÷ 2 = 6.28. Straight sides: 4 + 5 + 5 = 14. Total: 14 + 6.28 = 20.28 m. The top of the rectangle is inside the shape, so it is not counted.
Two semicircles make one full circle: 3.14 × 10 = 31.4. Two straight sides: 2 × 20 = 40. 40 + 31.4 = 71.4 cm. The dashed lines are inside, so they are not counted.
Two semicircles make one full circle: 3.14 × 14 = 43.96. Two straight sides: 2 × 30 = 60. 60 + 43.96 = 103.96 m. The dashed lines are inside, so they are not counted.

items.q: A semicircle is cut out of the top of this rectangle. Find the perimeter of the shape that is left. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Rectangle: 2 × (12 + 8) = 40. Take away the 6 cm gap: 40 − 6 = 34. Add the curved edge 3.14 × 6 ÷ 2 = 9.42: 34 + 9.42 = 43.42 cm.

items.q: A semicircle is cut out of the top of this rectangle. Find the perimeter of the shape that is left. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Rectangle: 2 × (16 + 10) = 52. Take away the 8 m gap: 52 − 8 = 44. Add the curved edge 3.14 × 8 ÷ 2 = 12.56: 44 + 12.56 = 56.56 m.

items.q: How can you find the area of a composite shape?
c: Multiply its longest side by its shortest side
Split it into simple shapes, then add or subtract their areas
Add the lengths of all its sides
Multiply all the labelled sides together
items.e: Split it into simple shapes (rectangles, triangles, semicircles). Add the parts, or subtract a part that is cut out.

items.q: Which formula gives the area of a semicircle with radius r?
items.e: A semicircle is half a circle, so its area is half of πr²: A = π × r × r ÷ 2. π × d ÷ 2 is the length of its curved edge.

items.q: Find the area of this shape.
items.e: Whole rectangle: 11 × 8 = 88. Corner cut out: 5 × 3 = 15. 88 − 15 = 73 cm². (103 adds two rectangles that overlap, so a part is counted twice.)

items.q: Find the area of this shape.
items.e: Whole rectangle: 14 × 10 = 140. Corner cut out: 6 × 4 = 24. 140 − 24 = 116 m². (164 adds two rectangles that overlap, so a part is counted twice.)

items.q: Find the area of this shape.
items.e: Whole rectangle: 12 × 7 = 84. Corner cut out: 4 × 3 = 12. 84 − 12 = 72 cm². (104 adds two rectangles that overlap, so a part is counted twice.)

items.q: Find the area of this shape.
items.e: Whole rectangle: 16 × 12 = 192. Corner cut out: 7 × 5 = 35. 192 − 35 = 157 m². (220 adds two rectangles that overlap, so a part is counted twice.)

items.q: Find the area of this house shape.
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 5 = 40. Triangle: ½ × 8 × 3 = 12 (use the height 3, not the sloped side). 40 + 12 = 52 m².

items.q: Find the area of this house shape.
items.e: Rectangle: 12 × 6 = 72. Triangle: ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 (use the height 8, not the sloped side). 72 + 48 = 120 cm².

items.q: Find the area of this house shape.
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 4 = 24. Triangle: ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 (use the height 4, not the sloped side). 24 + 12 = 36 m².

items.q: A shape is a rectangle 8 cm wide and 5 cm tall with a semicircle on the 8 cm side. Find its area. Use π ≈ 3.14.

items.e: Rectangle: 20 × 10 = 200. Two semicircles make one circle with r = 5: 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 78.5. 200 + 78.5 = 278.5 cm².
Rectangle: 30 × 14 = 420. Two semicircles make one circle with r = 7: 3.14 × 7 × 7 = 153.86. 420 + 153.86 = 573.86 m².

items.q: A semicircle is cut out of this rectangle. Find the area of the shape that is left. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Rectangle: 12 × 8 = 96. Semicircle: r = 3, so 3.14 × 3 × 3 ÷ 2 = 14.13. The semicircle is cut out, so subtract: 96 − 14.13 = 81.87 cm².

items.q: A semicircle is cut out of this rectangle. Find the area of the shape that is left. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Rectangle: 16 × 10 = 160. Semicircle: r = 4, so 3.14 × 4 × 4 ÷ 2 = 25.12. The semicircle is cut out, so subtract: 160 − 25.12 = 134.88 m².

items.q: A picture frame is a 30 cm by 24 cm rectangle with a 20 cm by 14 cm opening in the middle. What is the area of the frame?
items.e: Outside rectangle: 30 × 24 = 720. Opening: 20 × 14 = 280. Frame: 720 − 280 = 440 cm².

items.q: A picture frame is a 40 cm by 30 cm rectangle with a 30 cm by 16 cm opening in the middle. What is the area of the frame?
items.e: Outside rectangle: 40 × 30 = 1200. Opening: 30 × 16 = 480. Frame: 1200 − 480 = 720 cm².

items.q: A rectangle is 10 m by 6 m. A right triangle with legs of 4 m and 3 m is cut off one corner. What is the area that is left?
items.e: Rectangle: 10 × 6 = 60 m². Triangle: ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 m². 60 − 6 = 54 m². 48 m² forgets the ½ for the triangle.

items.q: An ice cream cone shape is a triangle with a base of 8 cm and a height of 12 cm, with a semicircle (diameter 8 cm) on the base. Find the total area. Use π ≈ 3.14.

sets.title: Volume of composite prisms and cylinders

items.q: How do you find the volume of a composite solid?
c: Multiply all the labelled lengths together
Add the areas of all its faces
Add the volumes of its parts, or subtract a part that is removed
Find the volume of the largest part only
items.e: Split the solid into prisms and cylinders. Add their volumes, or subtract a part that is cut out. Adding the areas of the faces gives the surface area.

items.q: A prism has the same shape all the way through. Which rule gives its volume?
items.e: Every slice of a prism is the same shape as its base, so V = area of the base × length (or height). This works for any base, even an L shape or a house shape.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms. Find its volume.
items.e: Bottom prism: 10 × 5 × 5 = 250 (its height is 8 − 3 = 5). Top prism: 4 × 5 × 3 = 60. 250 + 60 = 310 cm³.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms. Find its volume.
items.e: Bottom prism: 12 × 6 × 5 = 360 (its height is 9 − 4 = 5). Top prism: 5 × 6 × 4 = 120. 360 + 120 = 480 cm³.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms. Find its volume.
items.e: Bottom prism: 8 × 10 × 4 = 320 (its height is 6 − 2 = 4). Top prism: 3 × 10 × 2 = 60. 320 + 60 = 380 m³.

items.q: This solid is made of two rectangular prisms. Find its volume.
items.e: Bottom prism: 15 × 8 × 6 = 720 (its height is 10 − 4 = 6). Top prism: 5 × 8 × 4 = 160. 720 + 160 = 880 cm³.

A mailbox is a box with half a cylinder on top. Find its volume. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Front: rectangle 20 × 15 = 300, plus a semicircle 3.14 × 10 × 10 ÷ 2 = 157. Front area: 457 cm². Volume: 457 × 40 = 18 280 cm³.

items.q: This solid is a box with half a cylinder on top. Find its volume. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Front: rectangle 10 × 6 = 60, plus a semicircle 3.14 × 5 × 5 ÷ 2 = 39.25. Front area: 99.25 cm². Volume: 99.25 × 30 = 2977.5 cm³.

items.q: A storage shed is a box with half a cylinder for a roof. Find its volume. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Front: rectangle 4 × 3 = 12, plus a semicircle 3.14 × 2 × 2 ÷ 2 = 6.28. Front area: 18.28 m². Volume: 18.28 × 10 = 182.8 m³.

items.q: One cylinder sits on top of another. Find the total volume. Use π ≈ 3.14.

A wooden cube with 10 cm edges has a round hole drilled straight through it. The hole has a radius of 2 cm. What volume of wood is left? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Block: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000 cm³. Hole: 3.14 × 2 × 2 × 10 = 125.6 cm³. The hole is removed, so subtract: 1000 − 125.6 = 874.4 cm³.

items.q: A block is 20 cm long, 12 cm wide and 5 cm high. A round hole with a diameter of 6 cm goes straight down through it (5 cm deep). What volume is left? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Block: 20 × 12 × 5 = 1200 cm³. Hole: r = 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so 3.14 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 141.3 cm³. The hole is removed, so subtract: 1200 − 141.3 = 1058.7 cm³.

items.q: A trophy has a cylinder (radius 3 cm, height 5 cm) on top of a 10 cm × 10 cm × 4 cm box. Find its total volume. Use π ≈ 3.14.
A solid is half of a cylinder. The cylinder had a radius of 5 cm and a length of 20 cm. Find the volume of the half. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Whole cylinder: 3.14 × 5 × 5 × 20 = 1570 cm³. Half: 1570 ÷ 2 = 785 cm³.

items.q: A pipe is a cylinder with a hole through the middle. The outside radius is 5 cm, the inside radius is 3 cm and the pipe is 10 cm long. What volume of material is in the pipe? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Outside cylinder: 3.14 × 5 × 5 × 10 = 785 cm³. Hole: 3.14 × 3 × 3 × 10 = 282.6 cm³. 785 − 282.6 = 502.4 cm³. (Using r = 5 − 3 = 2 gives only 125.6 cm³.)

items.q: What is the surface area of a solid?
c: the total area of all its faces
items.e: Surface area is the total area of all its faces (like the paper needed to wrap it). The space inside is the volume.

items.q: Two solids are glued together face to face. What happens to the faces that touch?
c: They are added to the volume
They are hidden, so they are not part of the surface area
items.e: The faces that touch are inside the new solid. Nobody could paint them, so they are not part of the surface area. Subtract the touching area from both solids.

items.q: The curved surface of a cylinder is unrolled. Which shape does it make?
c: a rectangle as long as the circumference
a rectangle as long as the radius
items.e: Unrolled, the curved surface is a rectangle. One side is the height; the other is the circumference 2πr. So its area is 2πr × h.

A cylinder has a diameter of 10 cm and a height of 20 cm. Find its surface area. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: r = 5 cm. Two circles: 2 × 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 157 cm². Curved surface: 3.14 × 10 × 20 = 628 cm². 157 + 628 = 785 cm².

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles with sides 3, 4 and 5 cm. Find its surface area.
items.e: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 3 × 4 = 12. Three rectangles: (3 + 4 + 5) × 10 = 120. 12 + 120 = 132 cm². Do not forget the sloped face (5 cm wide).

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles with sides 6, 8 and 10 cm. Find its surface area.
items.e: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 6 × 8 = 48. Three rectangles: (6 + 8 + 10) × 15 = 360. 48 + 360 = 408 cm². Do not forget the sloped face (10 cm wide).

items.q: An open box (no lid) is 30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 10 cm high. What is the area of cardboard needed to make it?
An open box (no lid) is 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. What is the area of cardboard needed to make it?
A cube sits on top of a box. Find the surface area of the whole solid.
items.e: Box: 304. Cube: 6 × 4 × 4 = 96. The touching faces (4 × 4 = 16) are hidden on the box and on the cube: 304 + 96 − 2 × 16 = 368 cm².

items.q: A cube sits on top of a box. Find the surface area of the whole solid.
items.e: Box: 460. Cube: 6 × 6 × 6 = 216. The touching faces (6 × 6 = 36) are hidden on the box and on the cube: 460 + 216 − 2 × 36 = 604 cm².

items.q: A cube sits on top of a box. Find the surface area of the whole solid.
items.e: Box: 1600. Cube: 6 × 10 × 10 = 600. The touching faces (10 × 10 = 100) are hidden on the box and on the cube: 1600 + 600 − 2 × 100 = 2000 cm².

items.q: Find the surface area of this solid. (Hint: 2 × front area + perimeter of the front × depth.)
items.e: Front: 12 × 5 + 5 × 3 = 75 cm². Perimeter of the front: all 6 sides = 40 cm. 2 × 75 + 40 × 6 = 150 + 240 = 390 cm².

items.q: A shed is shaped like a house: the front is an 8 m by 5 m rectangle with a triangle on top (height 3 m, sloped sides 5 m). The shed is 10 m long. Find its surface area, including the floor.
A cylinder (radius 5 cm, height 5 cm) is glued on top of a bigger cylinder (radius 10 cm, height 5 cm). Find the surface area of the whole solid. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Big cylinder: 2 × 314 + 314 = 942 cm². Small: 2 × 78.5 + 157 = 314 cm². The touching circle (78.5 cm²) is hidden on both: 942 + 314 − 2 × 78.5 = 1099 cm².

sets.title: Word problems: tracks, pools and houses

items.q: Hana’s garden is a 6 m by 4 m rectangle with a semicircle on one 4 m side. She puts a fence all the way around it. How much fence does she need? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Straight sides: 6 + 6 + 4 = 16 m (the side the semicircle sits on is not fenced). Curve: 3.14 × 4 ÷ 2 = 6.28 m. 16 + 6.28 = 22.28 m.
The two semicircles make one circle: 3.14 × 60 = 188.4 m. 100 + 100 + 188.4 = 388.4 m.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, Kai wants to run at least 2 km on that track (one lap is 388.4 m). How many full laps must he run?
items.e: 2 km = 2000 m. 2000 ÷ 388.4 ≈ 5.15. Five laps are only 1942 m, so he needs 6 laps.

items.q: The grass field inside the same track is a 100 m by 60 m rectangle with a semicircle on each end (diameter 60 m). What is the area of the grass? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Rectangle: 100 × 60 = 6000 m². Two semicircles = one circle with r = 30: 3.14 × 30 × 30 = 2826 m². 6000 + 2826 = 8826 m².

items.q: A window at the cottage is a rectangle 1.2 m wide and 1.5 m tall with a semicircle on top. Wood trim goes around the outside. How long is the trim? Use π ≈ 3.14.
A dog run is a 10 m by 8 m rectangle with a semicircle on one 8 m side. Fencing costs $15 per metre. How much does the fence around the outside cost? Use π ≈ 3.14.
A backyard pool is an 8 m by 4 m rectangle with a semicircle on one 4 m end. What area does a pool cover need to have? Use π ≈ 3.14.
The end wall of a house is an 8 m by 3 m rectangle with a triangle on top (height 3 m). It has a door 1 m by 2 m. How much wall area needs paint?
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 3 = 24 m². Triangle: ½ × 8 × 3 = 12 m². Wall: 36 m². Take away the door (1 × 2 = 2 m²): 36 − 2 = 34 m².

items.q: Mateo paints two end walls of 34 m² each. One can of paint covers 10 m². How many cans must he buy?
items.e: Total: 2 × 34 = 68 m². 68 ÷ 10 = 6.8. Six cans are not enough, so he buys 7 cans.

items.q: A house is 8 m wide and 10 m long. Its roof is 3 m high at the peak, and each of its two rectangular sides is 5 m from the peak down to the edge. What area of shingles covers the whole roof?
items.e: Each side: 5 × 10 = 50 m². Two sides: 2 × 50 = 100 m². (60 m² uses the roof height 3 m instead of the sloped length 5 m.)

items.q: A house is 8 m wide and 10 m long. The walls are 3 m high, and the roof is a triangular prism 3 m high. What is the volume of the house, including the attic?
items.e: Walls part: 8 × 10 × 3 = 240 m³. Attic: ½ × 8 × 3 × 10 = 120 m³. 240 + 120 = 360 m³. 480 m³ forgets the ½ for the triangle.

items.q: A pool is 10 m wide. The side view below shows the water. How many litres of water does the pool hold?
A backyard rink is a 12 m by 6 m rectangle with a semicircle on each 6 m end. Owen floods it with water 5 cm deep. How many litres of water does he need? Use π ≈ 3.14.
An L-shaped sandbox is a 3 m by 2 m rectangle with a 1 m by 1 m corner cut out. Sand fills it 30 cm deep. What volume of sand is needed?
Concrete steps have 3 steps. Each step is 30 cm deep and 20 cm high, and the steps are 1 m wide. The steps are solid concrete down to the ground. What volume of concrete is needed?
A water trough at a farm is half a cylinder with a diameter of 60 cm and a length of 2 m. How many litres does it hold when full? Use π ≈ 3.14.
A soup can has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 11 cm. The paper label covers only the curved side. What is the area of the label? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: The label unrolls into a rectangle: circumference × height = 2 × 3.14 × 4 × 11 = 276.32 cm². The top and bottom are not covered.

items.q: A tent is a triangular prism 3 m long. Each triangle end has a base of 2.4 m and a height of 1.6 m, and each sloped side is 2 m wide. The tent has no floor. How much fabric is needed?
items.e: Two triangles: 2 × ½ × 2.4 × 1.6 = 3.84 m². Two sloped sides: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12 m². 3.84 + 12 = 15.84 m².

items.q: A two-layer birthday cake has a bottom layer with a radius of 15 cm and a height of 10 cm, and a top layer with a radius of 10 cm and a height of 8 cm. Icing covers the top and the sides, but not the bottom. What area is iced? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Seen from above, the tops together make one circle of r = 15: 3.14 × 15 × 15 = 706.5 cm². Sides: 2 × 3.14 × 15 × 10 + 2 × 3.14 × 10 × 8 = 942 + 502.4 = 1444.4 cm². 706.5 + 1444.4 = 2150.9 cm².

items.q: A concrete culvert pipe is 2 m long. Its outside radius is 0.5 m and its inside radius is 0.4 m. What volume of concrete is in the pipe? Use π ≈ 3.14.
